The column encoding covers every actual matchingSection 1’s six symbols exhaust the possibilities at every vertex:An unoccupied vertex receives 0.A selected vertex receives 1.A matching endpoint receives the symbol specifying its unique actual mate: left, right, below, or above.Every ordinary grid edge has one of those directions. The reciprocal 4,5 requirements enforce genuine vertical pairs, and their boundary checks exclude downward mates from the last row and upward mates from the first row.The code implements those conditions correctly. In particular, Python’s short-circuit evaluation protects the word[r+1] and word[r-1] accesses at the row boundaries.For horizontal edges,

pairs endpoints across the boundary in exactly the same row. Each vertex has one symbol, so a newly introduced endpoint already matched left cannot also be matched right or vertically. Thus the adapter respects the matching’s exclusive use of endpoints.The first-column requirement  $L=\varnothing$  and final requirement  $R=\varnothing$  ensure that every represented matching edge stays inside the board.The only local degree rejection concerns selected vertices with two occupied vertical neighbours. Arbitrary adjacencies among matching endpoints remain permitted. Consequently, the encoding preserves the full class of matchings in the question.3. Its possible interpretations have the same future constraint:A matching endpoint whose mate has already been accounted for permits either occupancy status at its right neighbour.A selected vertex with zero occupied neighbours so far also permits either occupancy status at its right neighbour.For the selected vertex, the right neighbour is its only remaining neighbour to examine. Its selected status can therefore be forgotten once its weight has been counted and its membership in  $F$  has been determined.For a new selected vertex, let  $d_v$  be its number of occupied vertical neighbours and let  $\ell\in\{0,1\}$  indicate an occupied left neighbour. Endpoint accounting and potential cancellation prevent reuseFor column  $k$ , its weight is
$$a_k=2|T_k|+|P_k|,$$
where  $P_k$  is the set of actual matching endpoints in that column. Therefore
$$\sum_{k=1}^{w}a_k
=
2|T|+|P|
=
2(|T|+|M|).$$
A horizontal matching edge contributes one unit at its left endpoint and one at its right endpoint. Together these give the required two units for one matching edge in the doubled objective. Vertical matching edges contribute their two endpoint units within one column.Each endpoint belongs to exactly one column and has exactly one matching role. In particular, an endpoint consumed as a left mate cannot also become a right mate. Selected obligations and outgoing matching endpoints are disjoint because  $F\cap R=\varnothing$ .The potential accounting also uses each boundary exactly once. With  $\Phi_k$  the phase-appropriate potential, a transition gives
$$a_{k+1}-6\le \Phi_{k+1}-\Phi_k.$$
Summing cancels every internal potential once with each sign. The proof uses one joint state for the entire six-row boundary, so interactions between rows are included in the same inequality. It makes no separate allocation of boundary slack to multiple components.6. The induction and sharpness arguments cover arbitrary lengthThe separate seed is essential and correctly supplied. The actual table has
$$E(\varnothing)=-4,\qquad Q(\varnothing)=-6.$$
The proof starts directly from
$$a_1-6\le Q(s_1).$$
For an arbitrary feasible board, set
$$C_k=\sum_{i=1}^{k}a_i,\qquad
\Phi_k=
\begin{cases}
E(s_k),&k\text{ even},\\
Q(s_k),&k\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}$$
The seed gives  $C_1-6\le\Phi_1$ . If  $C_k-6k\le\Phi_k$ , the applicable checked transition inequality yields
$$C_{k+1}-6(k+1)
\le \Phi_k+a_{k+1}-6
\le \Phi_{k+1}.$$
This induction applies to every prefix of an arbitrarily chosen finite board. Its transition premise has no width parameter or upper-length restriction.At the final column,  $R(s_w)=\varnothing$ , so

=C_w
\le 6w+\Phi_w

starting with  $A$ . Since  $A\cap B=\varnothing$ , adjacent columns create no horizontal selected adjacency. An  $A$ -column contains exactly one selected vertical edge, between rows  $4$  and  $5$ ; a  $B$ -column contains none. Thus the degree condition holds, and
$$|T|
=
4\left\lceil\frac w2\right\rceil
+
2\left\lfloor\frac w2\right\rfloor

3w+(w\bmod2)$$
